lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Why must samples be about the same size/contact when comparing?

FEEDBACK
Different contact can fake insulator/conductor results; keep contact fair.

WATCH FOR
Touching both clips with your fingers while testing adds your body path and confuses results.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Fair-test ten materials. Results table + conclusion listing conductors found. Note any unsure results and why.

Write a short reflection naming one observation or step you corrected and why.

lesson.parent_notes:
Parent: Marking guidance for the independent task: Fair-test ten materials. Results table + conclusion listing conductors found. Note any unsure results and why. Accept equivalent original responses that show the same skill.

Parent: Written model 1: Original response on new material: Different contact can fake insulator/conductor results; keep contact fair. Reasoning: I used test by attending to material rather than copying the worked model.

Parent: Written model 2: Common error: Touching both clips with your fingers while testing adds your body path and confuses results. Correction: Different contact can fake insulator/conductor results; keep contact fair. Why: the correction restores accurate use of test.

Parent: Likely misconception: Touching both clips with your fingers while testing adds your body path and confuses results. Keep sample answers out of the child role.

Parent: Short-answer focus 1: Investigate or describe a fresh example (not the worked objects) that uses test. Record evidence and explain how it supports your claim.

Parent: Short-answer focus 2: Name one science misconception about test, correct it with evidence, and say why the correction works.

teach_steps.explain:
Testing materials in a circuit keeps the battery, lamp and connections the same while swapping only the sample in a gap.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner base claims on observation, fair tests and design evidence, rather than guessing from a picture alone. Keep every claim linked to what was seen or measured.

HOW TO WORK
Read the worked example and name the observations, properties or test steps that carry the idea. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. Compare your record with the feedback: did you use the same skill and show your evidence? If a result is uncertain, identify what would have to be observed or tested again. One deliberate, evidence-based revision is more useful than writing a longer answer.
